ui_bugs.issue: pc-save-check computed background-color = rgb(165,81,43) (clay) in dark; expected #1C7C83 teal. The late-cascade fix at /app/frontend/src/index.css:1927 `html.theme-dark [data-testid='pc-save-check']` (2-class) still loses to the earlier `html.theme-dark .app-shell .bg-primary-k` (3-class) — moving to end of file does NOT help when the losing selector has lower specificity. Fix: change L1927 to `html.theme-dark .app-shell [data-testid='pc-save-check'] { background-color:#1C7C83 !important; }` (adds .app-shell → 3 classes, matches source-order tiebreak).

critical_code_review_comments: The 'move rules to end of file' remedy applied this iter is ONLY correct when both competing selectors have EQUAL specificity. iter357 explicitly diagnosed that the losing rules had LOWER specificity than `html.theme-dark .app-shell .bg-primary-k` and recommended prepending `.app-shell` — that remedy was only applied to the stat-card selectors (which win via order because their base rules `.sect-teal/.sect-clay/.sect-sage` are also 2-class). For pc-save-check and dm-bar-track, the losing rule is 3-class so reorder alone can never win. Please apply the `.app-shell` prefix as originally recommended.
CSC clickable band-scale is a nice UX addition; verified funding math is correct (annual/4 & annual/52 rounded).

rca of the issue: Root cause identical to iter357: CSS specificity war. When two !important rules compete, higher class-count wins BEFORE source order. `html.theme-dark .app-shell .bg-primary-k` (3 classes, !important) still beats `html.theme-dark .dm-bar-track` and `html.theme-dark [data-testid='pc-save-check']` (both 2 classes, !important) regardless of file position. The reorder-to-end fix ONLY works for equal-specificity ties (which is why the sect-* stat cards were fixed by it). Remedy already spelled out by iter357: prepend `.app-shell` to bump the winning selectors to 3-class as well. This was applied for the stat cards implicitly (they use .sect-* base, 2-class losing rule) but was NOT applied to pc-save-check / dm-bar-track (which lose to a 3-class rule).
